title: Safeguarding academic integrity in the age of generative artificial intelligence across dental research, publishing, and clinical practice
html: Artificial intelligence (AI) in oral health care has been widely explored for its applications in clinical treatment planning, rapid and precise image analysis, dental claims processing, data analysis, decision-making support, and enhanced patient communication.1 Furthermore, the increasing use of AI in academic publishing provides significant benefits in scientific writing and research, including streamlined manuscript preparation, language editing, article structuring, rapid data analysis, and text translation, enhancing scholarly productivity.
